answer.label: Attributed to Jack Nicklaus
answer.sourceLine: Wikiquote’s sourced entry credits the line to Nicklaus in the International Herald Tribune, published in Paris on 28 February 1990 — weeks after his 50th birthday, which fits a joke about age and headwinds. We have not seen that issue, and no independent printing of the sentence turns up, so this is an attribution with a specific citation behind it rather than a verified quotation.

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: Nicklaus turned 50 on 21 January 1990, five weeks earlier
Attributed — the newspaper issue has not been consulted

source.excerpt: The older you get the stronger the wind gets—and it’s always in your face.
trail: The quotation and its citation come from the sourced section of Wikiquote’s Jack Nicklaus page ↗, which gives “International Herald Tribune (Paris, February 28, 1990)”.

The date is at least consistent with the remark: Wikipedia ↗ gives Nicklaus’s birth date as 21 January 1940, so the line would have been printed five weeks after he turned 50 — the year he became eligible for senior golf.

We could not consult the 28 February 1990 International Herald Tribune, and searches return only Wikiquote and quotation aggregators reproducing it. One citation, unread, is an attribution rather than a verification, and this page says so.
source.excerptNote: Wikiquote sets this with an em dash and no spaces; the form in wide circulation, and the one this page is titled with, uses a spaced hyphen. The words are the same.

author.metaLine: b. 1940 · American golfer, winner of 18 major championships
author.bio: Jack Nicklaus, born in Columbus, Ohio on 21 January 1940 and known as the Golden Bear, is generally regarded as one of the greatest golfers who ever played. He won 18 professional major championships and 73 PGA Tour events, the third-highest total in tour history. He founded the Memorial Tournament in 1976 at Muirfield Village, the Ohio course he co-designed, and has since built one of the world’s largest golf-course design practices.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: It is a golfer’s joke about getting old, and it works because the wind is the one opponent in golf that cannot be out-practised. A younger player hits through a headwind; an older one notices it. Nicklaus had just turned 50 when this was printed.

He was also, by then, the person with the most authority to make the joke. He had won the Masters at 46 in 1986 — the oldest champion in the tournament’s history at the time — which is the sort of record that earns a man the right to complain about the breeze.
detailsBody: A note on why this page stops at “attributed”. The citation is good: a named paper, a city, a precise date. But a single uncorroborated citation is exactly the shape that ages badly in quotation collections, because every later copy inherits the same unchecked root. Until the 1990 issue is read, the honest label is attributed.
If you have access to the International Herald Tribune for 28 February 1990 and can confirm the wording and context, that is the one thing that would move this page to verified.
context.pull: The wind is the one opponent you cannot out-practise.
